name: CapCut Chroma Video-In-Text Portal
use_when: A title, travel opener, section intro, or short-film transition should reveal moving footage through large text.
The word is short enough and bold enough for the background video to be visible inside the letters.
The transition can zoom through a letter into the next scene without confusing the viewer.
The editor needs access to CapCut text animations while footage plays inside the letters.
avoid_when: The phrase is long, thin, script-styled, or small, making the video inside the text unreadable.
The matte color is too close to colors in the destination video and chroma key will damage the image.
The text reveal would delay a short-form hook or cover important captions.
The chroma key leaves colored particles, holes, or edge shimmer.

timeline_pattern.pattern: black_background -> bold_short_text_in_key_color -> export_matte_or_compound -> overlay_on_video -> chroma_key_or_blend_text -> adjust_tolerance_or_blend -> optional_text_animation -> keyframe_zoom_through_letter -> hold_or_cut_to_scene
timeline_pattern.word_rule: Use one short word or a few large letters; the video needs enough letter area to read.
timeline_pattern.font_rule: Use a very bold font with thick letterforms before judging the effect.
timeline_pattern.matte_rule: Choose a key color that separates cleanly from the footage; test intensity so no colored pixels remain and no video detail disappears.
timeline_pattern.portal_rule: When zooming through a letter, choose a large open letter and land the zoom on a readable part of the destination video.
timeline_pattern.direct_mask_rule: When no text animation is needed, a text mask on the video layer is the fastest route.
timeline_pattern.animated_text_rule: When text animations are needed, compound a black background plus text matte, blend the footage into the text, then compound again so the text layer remains editable inside.

motion.rule: The zoom-through should be smooth enough to feel like a transition, then settle or cut once the viewer enters the footage.

keyframe_values.text_scale: Make the word occupy a large portion of the frame before export.
keyframe_values.zoom_target: Aim through a large letter opening or thick letter area that can fill the frame cleanly.
keyframe_values.tracking: Slight negative character spacing, such as -2 in CapCut, can tighten large portal words when readability remains strong.
keyframe_values.key_color: A light yellow/key color can work when it separates better than green for the chosen footage, but test per project.
keyframe_values.chroma_intensity: Raise intensity only until the matte color disappears; too much keying will erase desired video detail.

sound.rule: A soft whoosh or swell can support the zoom-through only if it lands on the visual move and stays below speech.

captions.rule: Suppress ordinary captions during the portal title if the title already carries the spoken phrase, then restore captions after the transition.

color.rule: The keyed text edge should be clean and not leave yellow/green fringe over the destination video.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render a text matte on black, use chromakey/colorkey or alpha extraction to create transparency, place it above the destination footage, and animate scale/crop toward the target letter.
implementation.remotion: Create a VideoTextPortal component with titleText, fontWeight, keyColor, matteRenderRef, chromaTolerance, zoomStartFrame, zoomEndFrame, and targetLetter metadata.
implementation.blender: Use text objects as masks or boolean/alpha mattes over video planes, then animate camera or text scale through the chosen letter.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Fast method: add the video, use Video > Mask > Text Mask, choose a bold font, tighten character spacing if useful, and place the text. Animated method: place a plain black background under editable text, compound them, place the fill video above with Linear Burn or a tested blend mode, compound the group, set the wrapper to Screen, then reopen the compound to apply CapCut text animations such as Random Rise.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics text as a track matte or render a colored text matte, key it with Ultra Key/Track Matte Key, then animate Motion scale/position through the letter. For editable animated text, use a nested text matte and apply animation presets inside the nest.

common_mistakes: Using a long phrase where the footage inside the letters cannot be seen.
Using a thin font that creates tiny video windows.
Turning chroma intensity too high and erasing the footage.
Leaving colored matte specks or edge fringe.
Zooming through a letter into an unreadable or poorly framed part of the footage.
Using the fast text-mask method when the edit needs text animation that only works on a real text layer.
Choosing a blend mode that makes the footage inside the text muddy or invisible.
qc: Is the word short and bold enough for the video to read inside it?
Does the chroma key remove the matte color without damaging the destination footage?
If text animations are required, is the editable text layer preserved inside the compound?
Are there no colored specks or edge fringe at delivery size?
Does the zoom-through land on a readable scene area?
Are captions suppressed or repositioned during the title portal?
